ratings_why.fun: One pile, one keyword and a clear overnight payout give three readable builds, and watching burials turn into stats next turn is a satisfying grow loop.
ratings_why.distinct: The shared pile that empties each turn and Fruit as a carry count are fresh, but the core is a familiar sacrifice-and-deathrattle tribe.

verdict_why: The cards read cleanly and the funeral-as-harvest fantasy is in the rules; the open items are wording tweaks and UI, not redesign.

points.text: Show the Compost tracker as the number each Fruit unit will gain tonight (a quarter), not only the raw pile, so a player sees the payout at a glance.
Printed versus current stats is the tribe's one hard read: when a unit dies, show what it adds to the pile, and badge Spores as always 1/1.
Hired Mute's 'since your last turn' should say plainly that shop burials and fight deaths both count.
Bellows Puffwell could name which pile he shares, e.g. 'your Compost as it stands now', since the pile grows during the fight.
Clerk Inkcap shrinking with each entry is a lovely read; adding 'for this fight' to the Health loss saves a trip to the rule notes.

standouts.why: Clerk Inkcap writes each death twice and grows shorter doing it: the seed's story is the card's rules.
Grandmother Bootlace is the network made literal, and burials cutting her run is a cost a player sees on the board.
Mourner of Three Rains turns the 'one rain or three' quarrel into a one-line rule anyone can read.

weakest.why: Moss-Bier Bearer is a generic 'neighbour dies, gain stats' unit with little Guild flavour of its own.
Rootbinder is blank text on a Guild-only board, so it reads as dead in most shops.
Hired Mute is a plain gold counter; the silent-mute fantasy doesn't show in what it does.

flags.note: Golden Mourner keeps the whole pile, so it grows every turn while every Fruit unit drinks from it.
Stacked Fruit from Sealbearers and Bootlace on one carry has no cap.
Amanita's Start of Combat order versus her neighbours' own Start of Combat needs to be visible to read.
